name: Intas Pharmaceuticals
desc: Large family-owned Indian pharma company making generics, biosimilars and contract pharma products, sold through its European arm Accord Healthcare.
markets: Plants in India and Europe; supplies hospitals and pharmacies in Europe, the US and elsewhere through Accord.
rationale: Large private pharma with worldwide sales and moderate consumer recognition in India and Europe; plausible but not obvious F1 fit.

name: KELIX bio
desc: Dubai-headquartered specialty generic pharma business developing and selling hospital-focused injectables and oncology medicines.
markets: Sells to hospitals, wholesalers and government tenders in the Middle East, Africa and Asia; privately held and relatively small.
rationale: Small B2B generics supplier with no consumer brand; modest regional interest, so weak F1 fit.

name: Neighbourly Pharmacy
desc: Canadian operator of community pharmacies across Ontario and other provinces that dispense medicines, give vaccinations and sell wellness items.
markets: Pharmacies across Canadian provinces, grown by buying independent pharmacies; no verified operations outside Canada.
rationale: Local pharmacy network with neighbourhood brand recognition and no international business; weak F1 fit.

name: Orna Therapeutics
desc: Massachusetts RNA therapeutics company developing engineered circular RNA medicines and lipid nanoparticle delivery for in vivo cell engineering.
markets: Based in the US; pre-clinical, venture-funded with ARCH Venture backing; no marketed products.
rationale: Early-stage RNA developer with no consumer profile, no products on sale and venture funding only; weak F1 fit.

name: Owkin
desc: AI company for biomedicine using federated learning to train models on hospital data, with partnerships including Sanofi, Servier and AstraZeneca.
markets: Headquartered in New York and Paris; sells collaborations and software, including the K Navigator assistant, to pharma and research customers.
rationale: AI brand with technology showcase potential, but B2B and little known beyond healthcare and AI circles; plausible but not obvious fit.

name: Point Biopharma
desc: Indianapolis clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing targeted radioligand therapies, including PNT2002 for prostate cancer.
markets: Operated from the US with manufacturing in the US and Canada before acquisition by Eli Lilly.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Senda Biosciences
desc: Massachusetts Flagship Pioneering platform company developing nanoparticle delivery systems made from naturally derived materials to carry drugs to specific tissues.
markets: Based in the US; early-stage and privately held, targeting partnerships with pharma.
rationale: Early-stage private platform company with no consumer brand, no products on sale and venture funding only; weak F1 fit.

name: Sironax
desc: Clinical-stage biotech with US and China roots developing treatments for neurodegenerative and eye diseases such as glaucoma.
markets: Operations in the US and China; venture-funded and early stage with no products on sale.
rationale: Venture-backed pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile and no products on sale in any market; weak F1 fit.

name: Allen Institute for Brain Science
desc: Seattle non-profit research institute mapping the brain, including the Allen Brain Atlas, and publishing open neuroscience data for researchers.
markets: Based in Seattle; funded by philanthropy and grants; its open data is used by researchers worldwide.
rationale: Non-profit research institute with no products to sell; sponsorship would be unusual, so F1 relevance is very low.

name: Aptinyx
desc: Illinois clinical-stage biopharma that developed small-molecule NMDA receptor modulators for pain and neuropsychiatric disorders, spun out of Northwestern University.
markets: Operated from the US with no marketed products before winding down.
rationale: Wound down or bankrupt; no operations or marketing budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Cassava Sciences
desc: Texas biotech developing simufilam for Alzheimer's disease, which failed Phase 3 trials in 2024 amid scrutiny over data integrity.
markets: Operates from the US with no marketed products and a retail-investor shareholder base.
rationale: Pre-revenue developer with a failed lead drug and reputational issues; very weak F1 fit.

name: Chinook Therapeutics
desc: Kidney disease biotech developing atrasentan and other drugs for IgA nephropathy and other rare chronic kidney diseases.
markets: Operated from Vancouver and Seattle as a pre-commercial developer before acquisition by Novartis.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.
changed: Merged with Aduro Biotech in 2020; acquired by Novartis in 2023

name: Codiak Biosciences
desc: Massachusetts biotech that developed engineered exosomes as a drug delivery platform for cancer and inflammatory diseases, partnered with Jazz Pharmaceuticals.
markets: Operated from the US with no marketed products; failed to raise capital and went bankrupt.
rationale: Wound down or bankrupt; no operations or marketing budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Concert Pharmaceuticals
desc: Massachusetts drug developer using deuterium chemistry to modify existing drugs, with deuruxolitinib for alopecia areata launched as Leqselvi.
markets: Operated from the US with licensing income before acquisition by Sun Pharma.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: ESSA Pharma
desc: Vancouver clinical-stage oncology company that developed masofaniten, an oral androgen receptor inhibitor for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
markets: Based in Vancouver; pre-revenue; development of its lead drug stopped in 2024 and it has explored strategic options.
rationale: Pre-revenue company with a halted lead programme and no consumer brand; very weak F1 fit.

name: Paragon Biosciences
desc: Chicago biotech holding and company builder founded by Jeffrey Aronin that creates and funds specialised drug developers such as Emalex.
markets: Based in Chicago; privately held; portfolio companies have included gene-silencing, neuropsychiatry and rare-disease developers.
rationale: Private biotech holding company with a low public profile and no operating consumer brand; very weak F1 fit.

name: Ribon Therapeutics
desc: Massachusetts oncology biotech developing small-molecule PARP7 inhibitors, including RBN-2397, and other cancer therapies based on ADP-ribosylation research.
markets: Based in the US; privately held and venture-funded, with early clinical studies in solid tumours.
rationale: Private pre-revenue developer with no consumer exposure, no products on sale and venture funding only; weak F1 fit.

name: Singlera Genomics
desc: Diagnostics company developing cell-free DNA tests for early cancer detection and screening using methylation signatures.
markets: Operations in California and China; sells to clinicians and screening programmes rather than consumers.
rationale: Venture-backed diagnostics firm with a low profile; some China and US presence but weak F1 fit.

name: Univercells
desc: Belgian biomanufacturing group founded in 2014 that developed compact continuous bioprocess systems, notably NevoLine, for producing vaccines and biologics affordably.
markets: Customers are biopharma companies and public health bodies, with a focus on making vaccines more accessible in emerging markets.
rationale: Niche B2B biomanufacturing firm with little consumer profile; weak F1 fit despite its international customers.
changed: Technology unit sold to Merck KGaA in 2021

name: Zosano Pharma
desc: California specialty pharma that developed a microneedle patch system for skin drug delivery, with Qtrypta zolmitriptan for migraine as lead.
markets: Operated from the US as a development-stage company with no marketed product before bankruptcy.
rationale: Wound down or bankrupt; no operations or marketing budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Aiolos Bio
desc: San Francisco biotech developing AIO-001, a long-acting anti-TSLP antibody for asthma and other respiratory diseases, licensed from Jiangsu Hengrui.
markets: Operated from the US with no marketed products before acquisition by GSK.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Centogene
desc: German genetic diagnostics company offering rare disease testing and a biodata platform used by pharma partners for drug discovery.
markets: Operates across the Middle East, Europe and Asia; customers include physicians, hospitals and drug developers; loss-making for most of its history.
rationale: B2B diagnostics with no consumer brand and low public profile; some international reach but weak F1 fit.

name: Cyclerion Therapeutics
desc: Massachusetts neuroscience biotech developing soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators for central nervous system diseases, spun out of Ironwood.
markets: Operates from the US as a pre-revenue developer; cut programmes after trial setbacks.
rationale: Small pre-revenue developer with no consumer awareness and no products on sale after trial setbacks; very weak F1 fit.

name: Epic Sciences
desc: California cancer diagnostics company known for its circulating tumour cell platform and the AR-V7 prostate cancer test, sold to oncologists.
markets: Sells to oncologists, pharma trial sponsors and laboratories; privately held and venture-backed; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Private B2B diagnostics company with no consumer awareness and no international footprint known; weak F1 fit.

name: Fusion Pharmaceuticals
desc: Canadian radiopharmaceutical company developing alpha-emitting actinium-225 targeted therapies for cancer, with FPI-2265 for prostate cancer.
markets: Operated from Hamilton, Ontario as a clinical-stage developer before acquisition by AstraZeneca.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: HilleVax
desc: Boston vaccine biotech that developed HIL-214, a norovirus vaccine candidate from Takeda's programme; its main infant trial failed in 2024.
markets: Based in the US; pre-revenue; cut staff and sought alternatives after the failed trial.
rationale: Pre-revenue vaccine developer with a failed lead trial and no consumer exposure; very weak F1 fit.

name: Icosavax
desc: Seattle vaccine biotech developing virus-like particle vaccines against RSV and human metapneumovirus, based on University of Washington technology.
markets: Operated from the US as a clinical-stage developer before acquisition by AstraZeneca.
rationale: Acquired and absorbed; no independent brand or budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: MedAvail
desc: Canadian-US health technology company that built MedCenter self-service pharmacy kiosks placed in clinics, later moving to digital prescription fulfilment.
markets: Deployed kiosks in medical clinics in the US and Canada; loss-making and wound down in the early 2020s.
rationale: Wound down or bankrupt; no operations or marketing budget, so no F1 relevance.

name: Novan
desc: North Carolina dermatology biotech that developed nitric oxide treatments, notably berdazimer gel for molluscum contagiosum, approved in 2024 as Zelsuvmi.
markets: Operated from the US; filed for bankruptcy and its business was sold to Ligand Pharmaceuticals.
rationale: Wound down or bankrupt; no operations or marketing budget, so no F1 relevance.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2023; business sold to Ligand Pharmaceuticals in 2024

name: ProBio Inc. (GenScript ProBio)
desc: Contract research and manufacturing service for cell and gene therapy and biologics, offering plasmid, viral vector, mRNA and cell lines.
industry: cell and gene therapy contract manufacturer
markets: Sites in New Jersey, China and the UK serving drug developers; operates under the GenScript ProBio brand.
rationale: B2B outsourcing partner inside a Chinese life-sciences group, with no consumer profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Reneo Pharmaceuticals
desc: San Diego biotech that developed mavodelpar, a PPAR delta agonist for primary mitochondrial myopathies; its main trial failed in 2023.
markets: Operated from the US as a pre-revenue developer; reverse-merged with OnKure Therapeutics in 2024.
rationale: Pre-revenue developer that has reverse-merged into another company; no consumer brand and very weak F1 fit.
changed: Reverse merger with OnKure Therapeutics in 2024

name: SynOx Therapeutics
desc: Dublin clinical-stage biotech developing emactuzumab, a CSF1R antibody, for tenosynovial giant cell tumour and other inflammatory joint diseases.
markets: Based in Ireland; venture-funded and pre-revenue, with early commercial planning described.
rationale: Pre-revenue private drug developer with no consumer profile, no products on sale and venture funding only; weak F1 fit.

name: TrueBinding
desc: California early-stage biotherapeutics company developing galectin-3 antibodies for neurodegenerative disease and cancer, including an Alzheimer's candidate.
markets: Based in the US; privately held and venture-funded with no marketed products.
rationale: Early-stage private developer with no consumer profile, no products on sale and venture funding only; weak F1 fit.

name: Viva Biotech
desc: Shanghai contract research firm providing structure-based drug discovery, protein crystallography and chemistry services, plus equity investments in client pipelines.
markets: Serves pharmaceutical and biotech clients worldwide; revenue from fee-for-service work and licensing; listed in Hong Kong.
rationale: B2B research services firm with little public awareness; international clients but weak F1 fit.
